decision.title: Parsing XPath: fewer reductions, each text once per compilation (packet )

body.p: , after , , and . No public header changed; the ASTs and the IR are the same.

item.p: Whom it serves: every compile of a stylesheet or a Schematron schema, first EN 16931's, where XPath parsing was 32 % of the invoice transform and 30 % of the invoice validate from the .sch. Pays: about 206 KB of parse tables (the sxml command 16.93 to 17.14 MB), an AST copy per expression met again, a hash table per compilation.

Profile (callgrind, release, at ae61af90e): transform 1.618 x 10^9 instructions, sxml_xpath_parse 0.517, tree-sitter's parse of XPath 0.299 over 2,418 parses; validate 1.613, sxml_xpath_parse 0.483. The cost was per reduction, not per character: a typical assertion of 552 bytes and 116 tokens took 676 reductions, because each primary expression was reduced once per precedence level (22 hidden choice rules, A.5) on its way to an operand, each reduction a hidden subtree node the walk's cursor then passed through. Repeated texts matter less than their count says: the official stylesheet's 2,246 select, test, match and use attributes are 1,042 distinct texts, but the repeated ones are short (the distinct texts hold 93 % of the bytes).

Grammar (grammars/xpath, as cut XML's tokens and nodes): the hidden choice rules of the operator levels, the steps, primaries, literals, node tests and names are inlined (tree-sitter inline). They make no node, so node-types.json, every named node and field and the AST are unchanged; that assertion takes 132 reductions. _expression_single and _expression stay rules: inlining them doubled the states for 10 % fewer reductions. Regenerated with tools/generate-grammars.sh: xpath 1,179 to 1,609 states, xslt_pattern 1,275 to 1,706, value_template 1,166 to 1,596, xpath_full_text 1,559 to 2,117 (+48, +47, +48, +63 KB of tables). XQuery does not take them (inline is its Full Text rules only, its parser byte-identical to before): they gave it 5,647 to 9,518 states, +558 KB, for a parse a query makes once (xmark-all -0.15 %). The corpus tests of the five grammars pass.

The AST memo (sxml_ast_memo, src/xpath_ast.c; glossary ): an open-addressing table (FNV-1a, at most half full) of the ASTs a compilation parsed, keyed by the front end's entry point, the text and the parse's limits (expression depth, XML 1.1 reading), which are all a front end's AST depends on besides the source name; the static context does not enter a parse. A text met again takes a copy (sxml_ast_copy: the same capacities, node entries and text store, its own source name); a text in error is not kept, so each use reports its own error. The XSLT reader (src/xslt_read.c, one memo per read) and the Schematron builder (src/schematron_build.c, one per compile) parse every expression through it; it replaces perf-13's table of fixed texts and its node-by-node copy (, mechanism 3). Memory: one AST per distinct text more during a read, from the same allocator and limits; no recursion ().
The walk (src/xpath_parse.c): a named child's AST field is kept per grammar field identifier, a terminal's delimitation (A.3.2) per symbol, as kept kinds per symbol (-1.4 % of the parse).

Measured, instructions x 10^9 (callgrind, release; base ae61af90e and the change built alike from snapshots): invoice transform 1.618 to 1.323 (grammar) to 1.294 (memo) to 1.291 (walk), -20.2 %, sxml_xpath_parse 0.517 to 0.185 (14.4 % of the run), XPath parses 2,418 to 1,210; invoice validate 1.613 to 1.332 to 1.323 to 1.321, -18.1 %, sxml_xpath_parse 0.483 to 0.202, parses 2,323 to 2,248; the new benchmark xpath-parse (tests/bench/xpath-parse.xsl, 250 Schematron-style assertions, compile-bound) 0.947 to 0.649; xmark-all 8.641 to 8.638 (output equal). Processor seconds (fastest of 15, interleaved, a shared 4-CPU machine with other builds running): transform 0.212 to 0.185, validate 0.246 to 0.219, xpath-parse 0.121 to 0.093; the XT40 run (its compiles and transforms) 340.3 to 330.9, one run each, under other load.

Same result: a scratch harness parsed 133,165 texts with both builds (each QT4 test expression as XPath and as XQuery, the XT40 suite's select, test, match, as and value template attributes, the EN 16931 XSLT's and .sch files' attributes): the 119,276 that parse give identical node entries, text stores, capacities and roots; the 13,889 in error give the same status and code. 380 of those, all XPath, are located elsewhere, as tree-sitter's error recovery follows the tables (often at the "(" or "[" before the old place, or at the missing token after it), and 22 of them now say "The expression ends early or misses a token" for "The text is not valid XPath 4.0 syntax". tests/schematron_test.c's two pattern errors move from 4:16 to 4:20 and 15:46 to 15:47, the book's broken.sch from 4:20 "the text is not a pattern" to 4:30 "the pattern is incomplete" (the "]" missing at the end), and three CLI tests' XTSE0340 for match="item[" and context="line[" from the pattern's start to its "[" (5:18 to 5:22, 4:16 to 4:20). Conformance setup: base ae61af90e and the change built alike (preset , snapshots), run one after the other on the same machine with TZ, LANG and LC_ALL unset, from each snapshot's root: sxml-qt4 run --spec=XP40 --format=json, sxml-qt4 run --spec=XQ40 --format=json, sxml-xslt-test run --format=json (default catalogs, no test list). XP40 32,785, XQ40 46,114 and XT40 12,185 passed in both: 0 outcomes differ, case by case. 7.30's suite (sxml-schematron-test run): 463 passed, 3 failed, 43 implementation-defined, 5 not applicable, each case as before; VEFA (run_vefa.py with the official EN 16931 UBL XSLT, and sxml-schematron-test vefa with the .sch, over the Invoice and CreditNote unit tests) 1,133 of 1,133 checks. The IR text form after the passes (src/ir.c's printer, dumped by a scratch-only hook in sxml_ir_run_passes, as in ) is byte-identical on the EN 16931 stylesheet (141 MB of text), on the unit compiled from its .sch, on xpath-parse, and on all 414,483 units the XT40 suite compiles (an FNV-1a hash and length per unit, in order). New unit tests in tests/xpath_ast_test.c: the copy, the memo's keys, errors not kept, growth and every allocation failure. debug-gcc: 457 of 459 tests pass (kotlin/jvm and swift/linux skipped); clang-tidy clean on the changed files; tools/check-call-cycles.py finds no cycle.

Deviations: grammars/xquery/grammar.js (to keep its tables) and the regenerated parsers of grammars/xslt_pattern, grammars/value_template and grammars/xpath_full_text, which derive from grammars/xpath; src/xslt_read.c, src/schematron_build.c (the packet allowed them), tests/schematron_test.c, three files in tests/cli/expected/ and docs/book/src/schematron.md (the moved error locations).

Left: sxml.wasm was not built here (no WASI SDK); the tables add about 206 KB to it (the native libraries' growth), against the module's budget of 14,000,000 bytes (; 13,452,276 at ), so javascript/size_budget and its baseline need the owner's machine. In the parse that remains (0.185 of the transform) tree-sitter's own parse is 0.097 (lexing, the stack and subtrees per token, 24 reductions of _expression_single per assertion), the walk about 0.07 (each node's children are scanned twice, once for tokens and once by the cursor), and a parser made and deleted per text 0.005 ( keeps tree-sitter's memory to the parse step).
